title: dispatcher-hook mintDebt() is trusted input to V and windowEnd — malicious or buggy hook can over-commit emissions
asset_impact: Stakers' accrued rewards can be made unpayable (frozen behind _safePay revert) if the owner installs a hostile or buggy dispatcher hook whose mintDebt() overstates inflow vs. pull() actual.
attack_path:
1. Owner (or compromised owner key) installs a dispatcher hook whose mintDebt() returns a huge number but whose pull() mints little or nothing.
2. Natural user activity triggers _syncBudget + _recomputeSchedule; V = balance + hugeMintDebt inflates rewardBudget and windowEnd.
3. Stakers accrue against the inflated schedule; claims start reverting once balance < pending.
4. Recovery: owner topUp, or users take emergencyWithdraw (forfeiting rewards).
likelihood: low - requires owner action to install a bad hook; legitimate owner with well-behaved hook does not produce this loss.
assumptions: Owner is malicious or deploys an untested / buggy hook.
external_requirements: Owner key controls setDispatcherHook; no totalStaked==0 gate.
justification: Every attack path routes through the owner installing a hostile or buggy hook. Per C4 Universal Invalid + top-level CLAUDE.md ('centralization risks QA at best'), this is centralization. Surfaced as C rather than QA because the recommended fix is a concrete code change (cap V on pull delta, or validate mintDebt against pull inflow).
